question:
A 64-year-old male presents to the emergency department with sudden-onset shortness of breath and
palpitations lasting 2 hours. He works as a long-haul truck driver and recently completed a 1,000-mile
(1,600 km) trip. He has no significant medical history, takes no medications, and has no family history
of clotting disorders. Vital signs reveal a temperature of 36.7°C (98.0°F), heart rate of 88/min,
respiratory rate of 28/min, blood pressure of 131/80 mm Hg, and oxygen saturation of 94% on room air.
Physical examination is notable only for minimal bibasilar rales. A computed tomography pulmonary
angiogram (CTPA) confirms a segmental pulmonary embolism (PE). What is the most appropriate
treatment for this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Consult interventional radiologist for IVC filter
placement (B) IV heparin (C) Inpatient admission for unfractionated heparin (D) Outpatient
anticoagulation with rivaroxaban (E) Outpatient anticoagulation with warfarin and enoxaparin bridge (F)
Conservative management with aspirin therapy (G) Outpatient anticoagulation with apixaban (H)
Immediate surgical thrombectomy (I) Inpatient admission for tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) (J)
Observation for 24 hours with serial troponin measurements
 A. Inpatient admission for unfractionated heparin
B. Inpatient admission for tissue plasminogen activator (tPA)
C. Consult interventional radiologist for IVC filter placement
D. Outpatient anticoagulation with warfarin and enoxaparin bridge
E. Outpatient anticoagulation with apixaban
F. IV heparin
G. Observation for 24 hours with serial troponin measurements
H. Conservative management with aspirin therapy
I. Outpatient anticoagulation with rivaroxaban
J. Immediate surgical thrombectomy
